precepts.text: Solomon was wiser than Ethan, Heman, Chalcol and Darda, the sons of Zarah; he surpassed even the wise men of his own tribe.
precepts.point: Hezron begat Ram, Ram begat Amminadab, Amminadab begat Nahshon the prince of the children of Judah, and from Nahshon come Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Judah had five sons: Er, Onan and Shelah by the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess, and the twins Pharez and Zerah by Tamar. “The sons of Pharez; Hezron, and Hamul. And the sons of Zerah; Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara: five of them in all.” Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara became very famous. They were very wise.

How wise? Solomon’s wisdom is measured against them: “For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.”

Those same sons of Judah were so wise that many men were named after them, and Solomon surpassed even them. He was wiser than the wise men of his own tribe.

That is the house this genealogy runs through. Hezron, the oldest son of Pharez, begat Ram, and from Ram comes Amminadab, Nahshon, Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: a tribe of wise men, princes and kings.

precepts.text: The knowledge the Most High bestowed on Solomon exceeded that of all men who walked the earth.
precepts.point: He speaks of trees, beasts, fowl, creeping things, and fishes, and people of all nations come to hear his wisdom. Since his wisdom already excelled Egypt's, we have no need to dabble in Egyptology or any doctrine outside the scriptures given to us.

note.label: 1 Kings 4: Government, Peace, and the Wisdom That Excelled All

precepts.why:
Solomon speaks of what the Most High gave him: “For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements: The beginning, ending, and midst of the times: the alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons: The circuits of years, and the positions of stars: The natures of living creatures, and the furies of wild beasts: the violence of winds, and the reasonings of men: the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots: And all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.”

The knowledge the Most High bestowed on Solomon exceeded that of all men who walked the earth. That is why “he spake of trees, from the cedar tree that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall: he spake also of beasts, and of fowl, and of creeping things, and of fishes.” He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were a thousand and five, which is why we have Proverbs and the Song of Songs.

“Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt.” Since his wisdom already excelled Egypt’s, we have no need to dabble in Egyptology or any doctrine outside the scriptures given to us.

precepts.text: Solomon's wisdom and his three thousand proverbs and thousand and five songs mark him as the writer of this book.
precepts.point: The bride longs for the king's love, calling it better than wine; the savor of his good ointments makes his name as ointment poured forth, and therefore the virgins love him. Drawn into the king's chambers, they are glad and rejoice in him.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

precepts.why:
“The song of songs, which is Solomon’s.” Solomon is the author, not a woman, though that is the doctrine some try to push. The plain words say these songs belong to Solomon, and the history shows why. “And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore.”

His wisdom “excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt. For he was wiser than all men”, wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Chalcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol, “and his fame was in all nations round about.”

“And he spake three thousand proverbs: and his songs were a thousand and five.” Solomon was a poet, and his thousand and five songs mark him plainly as the writer of this book.

moments.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

points: And Solomon reigned over all kingdoms from the river unto the land of the Philistines, and unto the border of Egypt: they brought presents, and served Solomon all the days of his life. Solomon reigned over all kingdoms. So this was Israelite supremacy. That is how we are going to be again on the earth.
And Solomon's provision for one day was thirty measures of fine flour, and threescore measures of meal.
Ten fat oxen, and twenty oxen out of the pastures, and an hundred sheep, beside harts, and roebucks, and fallowdeer, and fatted fowl.
For he had dominion over all the region on this side the river, from Tiphsah even to Azzah, over all the kings on this side the river: and he had peace on all sides round about him.
And Judah and Israel dwelt safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
God gave Solomon largeness of heart as the sand on the seashore, and his wisdom excelled all the children of the east country, the Persians, the Indians and the Chinese, and all the wisdom of Egypt.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

points: Solomon is king over all Israel, and these are the princes he set: priests, scribes, a recorder, one over the host, one over the officers, one over the household, and one over the tribute. Twelve officers provide victuals for the king and his household, each man his month in the year.
This is the establishment of government, showing order. There is the king, then ranking men, each with a position of order, the same pattern of captains and officers set up in the days of Moses.

note.label: 1 Kings 4: Government, Peace, and the Wisdom That Excelled All

points: Judah and Israel are as many as the sand by the sea, eating, drinking, and making merry, and Solomon reigns over all the kingdoms from the river to the border of Egypt, who bring presents and serve him. Every man dwells safely under his vine and fig tree from Dan to Beersheba.
Israel dwells safely because of the wars of King David, who put down all the surrounding nations and put them to tribute. That is why Solomon is able to rule in a time of peace.

note.label: 1 Kings 4: Government, Peace, and the Wisdom That Excelled All

points: The Most High gives Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, largeness of heart as the sand on the seashore, so that his wisdom excels all the children of the east country and all the wisdom of Egypt. He is wiser than all men, speaks three thousand proverbs, and his songs are a thousand and five, which is why we have Proverbs and the Song of Songs.
